method.title: How ETFs are ranked
logic: Each fund gets 11 Barchart indicators. Every indicator is converted to a percentile against the watchlist's own distribution (so 50 is the median watchlist name), then the percentiles are averaged using the vote weights below. Score = weighted average percentile minus 50: 0 is a median name, higher is stronger.
Weights come from your vote table (360 votes = 100%): long horizon 65%, mid 27.5%, short 7.5%. RSI 100-day alone carries 27.8%. A fund needs at least 6 of the 11 indicators to be scored.
Asset floor for this tab: $10M, plus a 10-day average volume gate of at least 6,500.
steps: Start from every ETF listed in the market (US exchanges, or TSX / NEO / CSE for Canada) above the $10M asset floor (C$10M for Canada), plus a 10-day average volume gate of 6,500.
Keep long-only funds: no leveraged (2x or more), inverse, single-stock or single-commodity funds.
Fetch the 11 indicators from Barchart and score each fund against the watchlist distribution.
Rank by score and keep the top 50. Funds already on your watchlist are included.

method.title: How stocks are ranked
logic: Each stock is ranked from 1 (strongest) on the same 11 Barchart indicators and vote table as the ETFs, within every index it belongs to (S&P 500, S&P 400, Russell 2000, Russell Mid-Cap, SPI ADR for US; TSX 60, TSX, TSX Small-Cap, TSX Venture for Canada). Higher is stronger on every indicator.

The list is ordered by the weighted median of those 11 ranks (lower is stronger), using the best result across the indices the stock is in. The weight is how many votes that rank gets in the median. Weights are your vote table (360 votes = 100%): long horizon 65%, mid 27.5%, short 7.5%.

Top-20 in counts how many of the 11 indicators put the stock in the top 20 of its index. It is shown for breadth and does not change the order. HV is annualised historical volatility over 9 and 30 days.
steps: Pull the 11 indicators for every constituent from Barchart.
Rank each indicator within the index; missing values rank last.
The weighted median of the 11 ranks gives the median rank.
This page relaxes two filters to reach 50 names: the breadth floor (normally 6 of 11) and the mean-reversion filter (HV 9D divided by day change over 10). Lower ranks are weaker signals.

groups.sub: Names that sit below their 200-day average but have closed above the high they set 40 sessions ago: a base that is lifting inside a longer downtrend. One table per index.

method.title: How names are selected
logic: A name qualifies when all three hold on the latest close: (1) the close is below the 200-day average, the mean of the last 200 daily closes; (2) its z-score against that same window is below 0 (the distance from the average in standard deviations; it follows from the first test and shows how stretched the name is); (3) the close is above the intraday high of the bar 40 trading sessions ago.

Each index is screened on its own and tables are sorted by how far the close sits below the 200-day average. A name can appear in more than one table (for example in the Dow 30 and the S&P 100). TSX prices are in CAD, US prices in USD. Click any column header to re-sort.

groups.foot: Yahoo Finance daily prices as of 2026-11-27 (unadjusted for dividends). Universe: TSX 60 and S&P/TSX Composite from the iShares XIU and XIC holdings, Dow 30, S&P 100 and Nasdaq-100 constituent lists. Names listed in more than one index count once in the tab total.
